Number the coins $1,\dots,n$ with $n=7873$; odd positions start tails and must be flipped an odd number of times $v_i$, even positions an even number. The moves form a walk $p_1,\dots,p_m$ with $|p_{k+1}-p_k|=1$. Let $e_j$ be the number of traversals of edge $(j,j+1)$, so $m-1=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}e_j$.

Every internal even coin $2j$ must be visited, because coins $1$ and $n$ both have to be flipped; since $v_{2j}$ is even, $v_{2j}\ge2$. If $2j$ is not an endpoint of the walk then $e_{2j-1}+e_{2j}=2v_{2j}\ge4$; if it is exactly one endpoint, $2v_{2j}-1\ge3$; if it is both, $2v_{2j}-2\ge2$. The $(n-1)/2$ internal evens give pairs $(e_1,e_2),(e_3,e_4),\dots,(e_{n-2},e_{n-1})$, whose sums cover every $e_j$ exactly once. Hence $\sum e_j\ge 2n-4$, so $m\ge 2n-3$.

Parity of the alternating walk forces $m\equiv0\pmod4$ when $n\equiv3\pmod4$ and $m\equiv3\pmod4$ when $n\equiv1\pmod4$. Since $n=7873\equiv1\pmod4$, the bound $m\ge2n-3$ is admissible; for $n\equiv3\pmod4$ it would be raised to $2n-2$.

Construction. For $n=3$ use $1,2,3,2$ ($4$ moves); for $n=5$ use $2,1,2,3,4,5,4$ ($7$ moves). If a valid sequence for $N$ coins ends at $N-1$, appending $N,N+1,N,N+1,N+2,N+3,N+4,N+3$ adds $8$ moves, flips the two new odd coins once, and adds two flips each to $N,N+1,N+3$, preserving all parities. Induction yields $2n-3$ moves for $n\equiv1\pmod4$. Thus the minimum is $2\cdot7873-3=15743$.

candidates.text:
\boxed{15743}

Let $n=7873$ and write $O$ and $E$ for the total numbers of flips made on odd-indexed and even-indexed coins respectively.  
Initially odd coins are tails and even coins are heads, so every odd coin must be flipped an odd number of times and every even coin an even number of times. There are $\frac{n+1}{2}=3937$ odd coins (an odd number), hence $O$ is odd and $E$ is even.

Because successive moves are on adjacent coins, the parity of the flipped position alternates. Thus if the walk starts and ends on the same parity, that parity is used one more time. Since $O\neq E$, the first and last flipped coins have the same parity. If both are odd then $m=2O+1$; if both are even then $m=2E-1$.

Every even coin lies between two odd coins that must be flipped, so the walk visits each even coin at least once; by the parity requirement it visits each at least twice. Hence
$$E\ge 2\cdot\frac{n-1}{2}=n-1.$$
The even–endpoint case therefore gives $m\ge 2(n-1)-1=2n-3$, while the odd–endpoint case gives $m\ge 2n+1$. So $m\ge 2n-3=15743$.

This bound is attainable when $n=4k+1$ (here $k=1968$) by the walk starting at coin $2$:
$$2,1,2,\;\; \bigl(4j-1,4j,4j+1,4j,4j+1,4j+2,4j+1,4j+2\bigr)_{j=1}^{k-1},\;\; n-2,n-1,n,n-1,$$
which has length $3+8(k-1)+4=8k-1=2n-3$ and flips every even coin exactly twice and every odd coin an odd number of times.

Thus the minimum possible number of moves is $2\cdot7873-3=15743$.

\boxed{15743}

Let $f(i)$ be the number of times coin $i$ is flipped. We need $f(i)\equiv i\pmod2$ (odd positions start tails, even start heads). Coins $1$ and $N$ (both odd) must be flipped, and because the walk lies on a path, every coin $1,\dots,N$ is flipped at least once. Hence $f(i)\ge2$ for even $i$ and $f(i)\ge1$ for odd $i$.

Set $S_o=\sum_{i\text{ odd}}f(i)$, $S_e=\sum_{i\text{ even}}f(i)$, and $m=S_o+S_e$ (the number of moves). Then $S_e\ge N-1$ and $S_o\ge\frac{N+1}2$ with $S_o\equiv\frac{N+1}2\pmod2$. Since each move steps to an adjacent coin, the flipped positions alternate parity, so $S_o=\lceil m/2\rceil$ or $\lfloor m/2\rfloor$.

Minimising $m=S_o+S_e$ by taking $S_e=N-1$ forces $S_o\in\{N-2,N-1,N\}$. For $N=7873\equiv1\pmod4$ we have $\frac{N+1}2$ odd, so the smallest admissible $S_o$ is $N-2$, giving the lower bound $m\ge(N-2)+(N-1)=2N-3$.

This bound is attained by the walk
$$2,1,2,3,\;\underbrace{4k,4k+1,4k,4k+1,4k+2,4k+1,4k+2,4k+3}_{k=1}^{(N-5)/4},\;N-1,N,N-1,$$
which has length $2N-3$, flips each even coin exactly twice and each odd coin an odd number of times. Thus the minimum is $2\cdot7873-3=15743$.
